narrative: In Aleppo, a husband and wife in their twenties and thirties ran their lives: he owned a toy store and she worked in a shop. Life was already hard without water and electricity because of the fighting and destruction of the city, but it got worse in July 2015 when, during Ramadan, the different forces fought in Aleppo every night. They decided to take their two small children and leave. Their journey to Germany took 22 days, and many nights they slept on the streets. In the Hungarian camps their children, aged 4 and 7, were separated from them for two days and placed in separate cells. The Hungarian guards threatened the wife that they would take away her hijab if she did not let herself be fingerprinted. For the husband, the hardest thing about leaving home was saying farewell to his parents. Syria was their home, but he said the most important thing now was the future of their children.
